data.title: PayrollOrg® Announces 2026 Prism Award Winners for Excellence in Payroll Operations
data.description:
PayrollOrg® Announces 2026 Prism Award Winners for Excellence in Payroll Operations

PayrollOrg® Announces 2026 Prism Award Winners for Excellence in Payroll Operations

PR Newswire

SAN ANTONIO, Sept. 15, 2026

SAN ANTONIO, Sept. 15, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- PayrollOrg, the leader in payroll education, publications, and training, today announced the recipients of its 2026 Prism Awards. The annual awards recognize organizations that demonstrate measurable improvements and best practices in payroll management, processes, technology, and overall operations.

The 2026 recipients are:

  • Overall Payroll Best Practices: Booz Allen Hamilton

  • Management: GCE Global Solutions

  • Processes: PagerDuty

  • Technology: Lithia & Driveway

  • Honorable Mention: TFI International

"Payroll teams are continually finding new ways to improve how they operate and better serve their organizations and employees," said Dan Maddux, executive director of PayrollOrg. "The 2026 Prism Award recipients demonstrate the measurable impact payroll can make through stronger processes, strategic use of technology, and collaboration across the organization."

This year's winners delivered significant improvements to their payroll operations:

  • Booz Allen Hamilton completed a 17-month overhaul of its payroll ecosystem, automating 98% of inbound and outbound payroll data and reducing its payroll processing cycle from five days to three. A shift from arrears-based pay also reduced overpayments by more than 60%, saving $700,000 annually.

  • GCE Global Solutions implemented a new global operating model that reduced internal payroll escalation cycles by 45%, payroll processing time by 40%, and operational overhead costs by 35%.

  • PagerDuty modernized payroll operations across five countries and reduced payroll processing hours per cycle by 45% and global vendor processing fees by 20%.

  • Lithia & Driveway automated its payroll reconciliation process, an initiative projected to eliminate 5,000 hours of manual work and save approximately $130,000 annually.

Presented annually by PayrollOrg's Strategic Payroll Leadership Task Force, the Prism Awards honor payroll departments that demonstrate excellence and innovation. Previous companies recognized with Prism awards include Palm Beach State College, Cloudera Inc., ArcBest, Banfield Pet Hospital, and Bridgestone Americas.

The 2026 recipients were recognized during PayrollOrg's Payroll Leaders Conference, sponsored by Corpay Prepaid, in San Antonio, Texas. For more information about the Prism Awards, visit PayrollOrg online.

About PayrollOrg

PayrollOrg® (PAYO) is the leading global authority in payroll education, publications, and professional development. Established in 1982 as the American Payroll Association, PAYO provides payroll professionals and organizations worldwide with trusted education, training, certifications, certificate programs, publications, and compliance resources. Through its global network and industry expertise, PAYO advances the payroll profession, supports career growth, and helps organizations navigate the evolving demands of payroll compliance and management.

data.title: TCC Solutions® Celebrates 30 Years of Turning Complexity into Better Systems
data.description:
TCC Solutions® Celebrates 30 Years of Turning Complexity into Better Systems

TCC Solutions® Celebrates 30 Years of Turning Complexity into Better Systems

PR Newswire

INDIANAPOLIS, Sept. 15, 2026

Three decades of experience have shaped TCC Solutions into a specialized technology and consulting partner for state agencies and organizations that administer early care and education programs.

INDIANAPOLIS, Sept. 15, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- TCC Solutions®, an early childhood technology and consulting company, is celebrating its 30th anniversary in 2026. For three decades, TCC Solutions has partnered with government agencies and other organizations responsible for administering early care and education programs, helping them manage the policies, data and technology involved in running those programs and building systems that serve providers, professionals and families more effectively.

Founded in 1996, TCC Solutions began by providing technology and consulting services to organizations within human services. As the company evolved, it built an increasingly deep specialization in early care and education, pairing technology expertise with firsthand knowledge of the programs, policies, data and operational realities that shape the field.

That specialization led to Ascend®, TCC Solutions' configurable early childhood technology platform. Ascend gives agencies modern technology and integrated data capabilities that support core functions across the early education ecosystem, including: CCDF subsidy and Pre-k, child care licensing, workforce registry and training, Quality Rating and Improvement Systems (QRIS), and data and analytics solutions that connect information across systems and programs. Alongside Ascend, TCC Solutions provides program integrity initiatives and specialized consulting and professional services that help agencies put that technology to work within their specific programs.

"Our roots taught us early that technology is only one part of solving a complex problem," said Breht Feigh, President and CEO of TCC Solutions. "Over 30 years, we've continued to learn, evolve and deepen our expertise in early care and education. We understand the technology, but we also understand the programs, policies and people behind it. That combination has shaped who we are and how we work with our clients today."

As TCC Solutions enters its fourth decade, the company is focused on helping early care and education agencies respond to what comes next, from evolving policy and funding requirements to growing expectations for integrated data, interoperability, program accountability and easier experiences for the families, providers and professionals these systems serve.

That future will include continued investment in Ascend® and TCC Solutions' technology capabilities, as well as the specialized consulting, data and subject-matter expertise agencies need to turn technology into meaningful progress.

"The next chapter for TCC is really about building on what 30 years has taught us while continuing to evolve alongside the agencies and people we serve," said Melanie Brizzi, Vice President and Chief Growth Officer at TCC Solutions. "Technology will continue to change, policies will change and the needs of states and communities will change. Our opportunity is to bring the technology, expertise and partnership together in ways that help our clients respond to that change and build stronger systems for providers, professionals, families and children."

Throughout its 30th anniversary year, TCC Solutions will celebrate the clients, employees and partners who have contributed to its journey while sharing perspectives on the challenges, innovations and opportunities shaping the future of early care and education.

About TCC Solutions®

TCC Solutions® is an early childhood technology and consulting company. TCC Solutions helps government agencies run, modernize, and evolve the systems needed to support the complex landscape of early childhood funding, policy and programming. TCC's technology has been shaped by people who have worked for decades in the roles these systems are designed to support, helping agencies create stronger, more connected environments for staff, providers, families, and children. Alongside Ascend, TCC Solutions offers program integrity initiatives and specialized consulting and professional services that help agencies connect data and systems and better serve providers, educators, and families. Learn more at tccsolutions.com.

data.title: The best time to book your flight home for the holidays? Yesterday.
data.description:
By Genna Contino

'This is not going to be the year to tempt fate,' one travel expert says

Some consumers are expected to be priced out of holiday travel thanks to skyrocketing airfares.

Thanksgiving, Hanukkah and Christmas are still months away - but travel experts are advising those heading home for the holidays to book their flights now.

In August, airline fares were up more than 23% from the year prior, according to the U.S. consumer-price index - and flights are expected to keep getting pricier. The cost of jet fuel was at $4.32 a gallon as of Sept. 11, according to energy-information provider Platts, up 6% from the previous week and nearly 16% from the prior month.

Even those budgeting fall and winter travel this week will likely see elevated prices. While the cost of Brent crude oil (BRN00), which is used to produce jet fuel, dropped significantly in the summer, the price surged above $100 a barrel again last week after military escalation in the Middle East threatened to further tighten global oil supply.

Because pricey airfares haven't slowed travel demand thus far, airlines have been raising ticket prices over the past year to cover increasingly expensive fuel - and experts expect some consumers to be priced out of holiday travel altogether.

At the start of 2026, the average domestic airfare was $290, according to Kayak's airfare tracker; by Sept. 7, the average fare had skyrocketed to $397. Consumers are especially likely to feel the sticker shock when booking flights for busy travel days. Round-trip economy flights from New York City to Los Angeles, leaving the Wednesday before Thanksgiving and returning Sunday, ranged from $579 to $1,177, Google Flights showed Tuesday afternoon.

"Anyone planning to travel for Thanksgiving or in December should book their flights now to secure the lowest available prices," said Peter Vlitas, executive vice president of partner relations for international travel brand Internova Travel Group. "As flights fill up, fares increase significantly."

JetBlue's (JBLU) recent update to investors is one example of how airlines are passing higher costs on to consumers. The New York-based carrier reported higher fuel bills in a Sept. 10 filing, but said "strong underlying demand" is allowing the company to raise ticket prices to cover the extra expenses. The airline also noted that "early fourth-quarter booking trends also remain encouraging."

Katy Nastro, aviation and travel correspondent for the flight-tracker app Flighty, said even people who typically book budget airlines might be out of luck ahead of the holiday season.

"Even the cheapest of cheap flights, the Frontiers (ULCC) of the world, Allegiants (ALGT), there is no incentive there for them to keep those deeply discounted prices ... because they're feeling the impacts from jet-fuel prices just the same," Nastro said. "They don't have the luxury of the cash in the bank, like these bigger airlines do, to eat some of that cost."

Travelmation travel agent Mallory Dumond said she's been tracking holiday flights and has noticed that prices dip a bit on Tuesdays - but added that the pattern "is not a hard-fast rule" and she's seeing pricing starting to increase across the board. Dumond recommends that travelers planning to head home for the holidays use Google's flight-tracker tool to keep up with price changes. Even those who have already booked a flight should keep tracking it: If the fare does happen to drop, the airline could issue a voucher for the difference.

Don't Short Yourself: This hack can save you hundreds on airfare

If oil prices continue to increase, consumers won't just feel the squeeze from rising travel costs - food and gasoline prices are expected to climb as well. Operating on tighter budgets, Nastro expects some consumers to skip trips home for Thanksgiving to save money for a December flight, or opt out of holiday travel completely.

"This year, more than ever, it is so much more important to look forward, look to the next big travel moment, and get those plans locked in," she said. "This is not going to be the year to tempt fate."

-Genna Contino

This content was created by MarketWatch, which is operated by Dow Jones & Co. MarketWatch is published independently from Dow Jones Newswires and The Wall Street Journal. 




  (END) Dow Jones Newswires

data.title: American Rebel Light Beer Salutes First Responders at Black Oak's 25th Anniversary 9/11 Tribute Featuring Big & Rich, Craig Morgan and American Rebel CEO Andy Ross
data.description:
Big & Rich with Cowboy Troy, Craig Morgan, American Rebel (OTCID:AREB) CEO Andy Ross, and Jacob Smalley & The Morgan County Line united patriotic fans on September 11, 2026, to honor First Responders, remember the fallen and stand together for America.

A presenting sponsor of Black Oak Amphitheater - "Missouri's Premier Outdoor Concert Venue!" - American Rebel Light Beer thanks the venue and its fans and rallies support for upcoming concerts and the road to 2027.

NASHVILLE, TN AND LAMPE, MO / ACCESS Newswire / September 15, 2026 / American Rebel Holdings, Inc. (OTCID:AREB), America's Patriotic Brand™, today extended a heartfelt salute to America's First Responders and a red-white-and-blue thank-you to Black Oak Mountain Amphitheater - "Missouri's Premier Outdoor Concert Venue!" - following its September 11, 2026 concert commemorating the 25th anniversary of the September 11 attacks. Featuring Big & Rich with Cowboy Troy, Craig Morgan, Andy Ross, and Jacob Smalley & The Morgan County Line, the evening brought music and community together to remember the lives lost and honor the courage and sacrifice of those who answered the call.

American Rebel Light Beer is proud to be a presenting sponsor of Black Oak Amphitheater and to have been served to adult concertgoers throughout its 2026 season. From Memorial Day weekend to the September 11 tribute, the relationship has connected a proudly patriotic beer brand with a venue and audience that share its appreciation for great live music, community and love of country.

For American Rebel, the connection is unmistakable: great music, great beer and people who proudly love the USA. The Company encourages fans to carry that spirit forward by attending future Black Oak concerts, inviting friends, joining the Fan Club and helping spread the word.

American Rebel Light Beer, American Rebel CEO Andy Ross, Big & Rich, Craig Morgan and Patriotic Country Rock: A Night to Honor First Responders

Twenty-five years after the September 11 attacks, the occasion carried a meaning beyond the music. Black Oak brought its community together in remembrance of those who died, recognition of families whose lives were forever changed, and gratitude for First Responders and the men and women who continue to protect the nation.

In its public post-show Facebook message, Black Oak captured the spirit of the evening:

"Friday night was about more than great music. It was about coming together as a community to remember and honor September 11th and those whose lives were forever changed that day."

"A huge THANK YOU to everyone who joined us for an unforgettable evening with Big & Rich, Craig Morgan, Andy Ross with American Rebel Beer, and Jacob Smalley & The Morgan County Line!"

The September 11 performance marked a return to Black Oak for Ross, whose patriotic country rock was also part of the venue's May 24 Memorial Day weekend concert featuring Brantley Gilbert, Aaron Lewis and Payton Smith.

"Black Oak is our kind of place, and those fans are our kind of people," said Andy Ross, Chief Executive Officer of American Rebel Holdings, Inc. "We brewed American Rebel Light for patriots who love this country and what it stands for. Being part of Memorial Day weekend and returning for this September 11 tribute was an honor. The music brought us together, but remembering the fallen and thanking our First Responders gave the night its meaning."

Ross continued: "Black Oak doesn't have to be the biggest to be one of the best. To us, it is one of the premier - and most patriotic - venues in the Midwest. The management, the staff and the fans are exactly the people we are proud to stand alongside. God bless our First Responders, God bless our military and God bless America."

American Rebel Beer, Black Oak Amp & Andy Ross - 25th Anniversary 9/11 Concert

WATCH: Andy Ross Brings Patriotic Country Rock to Black Oak Amphitheater
Suggested video caption: Highlights from a night of live music, remembrance and American pride.

"Black Oak Amphitheater Is Back" - and American Rebel Light Beer Is Calling on Fans to Show Up and Drink a Rebel Light!

Black Oak's message did more than thank the audience. It asked the community to help sustain the venue's future:

"BLACK OAK AMPHITHEATER IS BACK IN BUSINESS - AND WE NEED YOUR SUPPORT!"

"Our new management team has invested an incredible amount of time, energy, and money into bringing Black Oak Amphitheater back and making it a venue that Southwest Missouri and the surrounding communities can be proud of."

"But we can't do it without YOU."

"Every time you share our posts, tell your friends, buy a ticket, bring your family to a show, or spread the word about Black Oak Amphitheater, you're helping us build the future of this incredible venue."

American Rebel Light Beer proudly echoes that call. Patriotic fans of great music and great beer: get behind Black Oak. Make plans for an announced show. Invite someone who has never been. Share a favorite concert memory and help another music lover discover the venue. Guests 21 and older can make an American Rebel Light part of the evening wherever it is available.

Supporting live music means supporting the people who book the artists, prepare the grounds, welcome the fans and make the experience possible. A great stage needs a great audience. Be part of the next crowd that makes it happen.

The Fans Said It Best: "This One Hit It Out of the Park"

In public comments on Black Oak's Facebook page, individual concertgoers described an experience that started before the main-stage performances and stayed with them after the music ended.

Rita Hobbs highlighted the welcome at the American Rebel Party Stage:

"It started right after passing through security and listening to the music provided at the American Rebel Party Stage."

She also reflected on the tribute:

"The displays of patriotism for the 25th anniversary of the 9/11 attacks by each group blew me away as well as the remembrances and displays in between the different bands and a great fireworks display."

Looking back on the season, Hobbs added:

"We have been to several shows out there this year and enjoyed them all, but this one hit it out of the park. Can't wait to find out what you've got going for next year."

Brittany Jo Maybee wrote:

"You all did an amazing job remembering 9/11. I can say from where we was sitting I was not the only one with tears rolling down my face."

Karen McNellis Doelger also looked ahead:

"We saw 3 shows this year and we're looking forward to next year."

Doelger described Black Oak as "our favorite outdoor venue." These individual reflections capture the connection American Rebel values: music that brings people together, occasions that mean something and a venue people want to visit again.

American Rebel Light Beer is a proud presenting sponsor of the Black Oak Amphitheater, Patriotic Black Oak fans shared their appreciation for a memorable evening of music and remembrance.

Missouri's Premier Outdoor Concert Venue! More Shows, More Music and More Reasons to Return

Black Oak's message made clear that its team is looking ahead:

"AND WE'RE JUST GETTING STARTED!
We're already working on our 2027 CONCERT LINEUP, and we're excited about what's ahead!"

The venue outlined its ambitions in four emphatic lines:

"MORE SHOWS
MORE GREAT MUSIC
MORE REASONS TO COME TO BLACK OAK
A STRONGER FUTURE FOR THIS INCREDIBLE VENUE"

Fans do not have to wait for next year to support the venue. Black Oak's published calendar lists ROCKtoberfest for Saturday, October 10, 2026, featuring Cody Parks & The Dirty South, Paralandra, Order of the Machine, and Whisper to Scream. Doors are scheduled for 5 p.m., with the show at 5:30 p.m. Fans should consult the official event listing for current details and ticket availability.

"Here's our message to everyone who loves great music, great beer and this country: show up for Black Oak," Ross said. "Buy a ticket to an upcoming concert. Bring your friends. Join the Fan Club and help spread the word. The people working to build something special there deserve our support - and the fans are what bring it to life."

Join the Black Oak Fan Club - Make Your Next Concert a Black Oak Concert

Black Oak invited supporters to stay connected:

"Want to be the first to hear about upcoming shows, special announcements, exclusive updates, and all things Black Oak Amphitheater? Join our Fan Club today! Visit our website to sign up and become part of the Black Oak family."

American Rebel encourages fans throughout Southwest Missouri and the surrounding region to follow Black Oak's official announcements, register for the Fan Club and plan their next visit. Check each event's arrival information, come early for scheduled pre-show entertainment and enjoy a night of music in the Ozarks near Table Rock Lake.

Upcoming concerts, tickets and Fan Club registration: www.blackoakamp.com

Official event listing: ROCKtoberfest - October 10, 2026

Follow Black Oak: Facebook.com/BlackOakAmp

Black Oak Amphitheater
1728 State Highway H, Lampe, Missouri 65681
Box Office: 417-202-7060
Box Office Hours: Monday-Friday, 10 a.m.-4 p.m., as listed in the venue's announcement.

Black Oak also emphasized:

"ONLY purchase tickets through our official website or by calling our Box Office."

American Rebel Light Beer is a Proud Presenting Sponsor of the Black Oak Amp. A Patriotic Audience. A Beer That Wears Its Values on the Can.

American Rebel Light Beer is built around a straightforward promise to its adult consumers: a great-tasting light beer and a proudly American identity. The brand puts its values right on the can:

"America's Patriotic - God Fearing, Constitution Loving, National Anthem Singing, Stand Your Ground Beer."

As a presenting sponsor, American Rebel Light Beer is proud to support Black Oak's live-music experience. Its connection with the venue reflects the Company's broader presence at concerts, motorsports events, football tailgates, community gatherings and prominent bars and entertainment establishments in its hometown of Nashville, Tennessee.

The Company has previously reported distribution agreements with more than 30 distribution partners across 18 states, supporting its efforts to make American Rebel Light Beer easier for consumers to find. The strategy pairs established wholesale relationships with retail support and in-person brand experiences. Geographic reach and distribution agreements are milestones, not a substitute for the day-to-day work of winning consumer trial and repeat purchases.

For American Rebel, Black Oak is a natural setting for that work: a venue with a passionate audience, memorable live entertainment and a shared appreciation for the USA.

Thank You, Black Oak: Honoring Our Heroes, Supporting Live Music and Standing Proud Together

Black Oak closed its post-show message with gratitude and an invitation:

"Thank you for believing in Black Oak, supporting live music, and being part of what we're building. We can't wait to see you in 2027!"

American Rebel extends its thanks to the venue's management and staff, the performers who took the stage, and the fans who supported Black Oak and enjoyed American Rebel Light Beer this season. Above all, the Company joins the community in honoring the First Responders whose service and sacrifice were at the heart of the September 11 remembrance.

The Company looks forward to opportunities to return and encourages fans to support Black Oak's announced events while watching for future programming.

Remember the fallen. Thank our First Responders. Share the memories. Support live music. Be there for Black Oak's next great night.

data.title: Lennar Unveils The Farm, a New Community Rooted in the Inland Empire's Outdoor Lifestyle
data.description:
Lennar Unveils The Farm, a New Community Rooted in the Inland Empire's Outdoor Lifestyle

Lennar Unveils The Farm, a New Community Rooted in the Inland Empire's Outdoor Lifestyle

PR Newswire

JURUPA VALLEY, Calif., Sept. 15, 2026

JURUPA VALLEY, Calif., Sept. 15, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Lennar, one of the nation's leading homebuilders, announces the debut of The Farm, a new resort-style community in Jurupa Valley, Calif., offering a diverse collection of low-maintenance condominiums and spacious single-family homes. With 16 thoughtfully designed floorplans to choose from, The Farm offers homebuyers a variety of options to suit their lifestyles.

"The Farm is about creating a neighborhood where life extends beyond the walls of the home," said Mark Torres, Lennar Inland Division President. "You can start your morning by walking through the community, spend the afternoon at the pool, meet friends for pickleball or a barbecue and come home to a space designed for the way you live. With a wide range of design options, we've created a community where buyers at many different stages of life can find their place."

Life at The Farm is designed around the simple pleasure of living outdoors and connecting with neighbors. Here, community is woven into the rhythm of everyday life—from afternoons spent poolside and evenings filled with pickleball or backyard barbecues to weekends exploring the parks, playgrounds and community garden. A thoughtfully designed clubhouse and dedicated dog park add even more opportunities to gather, relax and connect, creating a neighborhood where time together comes naturally.

Surrounding these shared spaces are four distinct home collections offering 16 condo and single-family home designs, giving buyers the flexibility to choose a home that fits their stage of life. Homes range from 845 to 2,869 square feet with one to four bedrooms and one-and-one-half to three-and-one-half baths, with pricing starting in the high $400,000s.

Every home at The Farm offers Lennar's signature Everything's Included® program, where the homebuilder's most popular features and finishes are built into the base price of the home. At The Farm, this includes stainless steel appliances, granite countertops, hard-surface flooring, cabinetry, and a host of other carefully curated interior touches and designer fixtures.

The Farm provides easy access to shopping, dining and entertainment just minutes away at Eastvale Gateway, The Station at Eastvale and Vernola Marketplace. Proximity to Interstate 15, SR-60 and SR-91 keeps commutes and weekend trips convenient.

For more information on these new home opportunities, call (855) 647-4939 or visit the community's website.

Lennar Corporation, founded in 1954, is one of the nation's leading homebuilders, dedicated to making the American dream of homeownership attainable for more people. Since its founding, Lennar has built more than 1.5 million homes for buyers at every stage of life in communities across the country, from first-time and move-up buyers to active adults. Lennar's Financial Services segment provides mortgage financing, title and closing services primarily for buyers of Lennar's homes. LENX drives Lennar's technology, innovation and strategic investments, shaping the future of homebuilding. For more information, visit www.lennar.com.

data.title: U.S. Treasury Auctions 20-Year Bonds at Highest Yield Since 1986
data.description:
By Paulo Trevisani 




  The U.S. Treasury on Tuesday auctioned $13 billion in 20-year bonds, with investors demanding the highest yield in four decades. 



  The bonds sold at a yield of 5.42%, the highest since January 1986, when it was at 9.45%. The 20-year was discontinued later that year before its reintroduction in 2020--and since that point, the highest yield until now had been 5.25% in October 2023. 



  Despite the elevated payout, demand indicators were on the soft side: the 2.57 bid-to-cover ratio was below the previous six-month average of 2.65, while the share acquired by the indirect-bidders group, which includes foreign investors, was also below trend, at 52.5%. 



  The tender results come as Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent is trying to cool down long-term yields by buying back more of the government's own debt. Earlier on Tuesday, he said in testimony before the House of Representatives that Treasury auctions have been the "most successful" in 20 years. 



  The 20-year yield rose to 5.418%, from 5.401% before the auction. Other maturities moved in tandem, with the 10-year rising to 5.014% from 4.996%.

data.title: City Kidz NexGen Animation Studios Taps Emerging Talent Zaria Weems as Voice of Jazzy Duval
data.description:
City Kidz NexGen Animation Studios Taps Emerging Talent Zaria Weems as Voice of Jazzy Duval

SCAD-trained multidisciplinary artist and Disney internship alum signs multi-year agreement as Jacksonville-based studio moves original City Kidz characters into full animation

City Kidz NexGen Animation Studios has selected emerging multidisciplinary artist and voice actor Zaria Weems as the voice of Jazzy Duval, a new member of the City Kidz crew, signing her to a multi-year voice acting agreement as the Jacksonville-based studio moves its original characters into full animation.

For Weems, 24, the opportunity goes beyond reading lines. City Kidz is giving her creative space to help shape Jazzy from the inside out, bringing her own energy, instincts and point of view to the character’s personality, attitude and unmistakable voice.

For City Kidz founder Pastor Clinton Bush, that is exactly what the studio and its NexGen Animation Fellowship were created to do: identify exceptionally talented emerging storytellers and creators, give them meaningful opportunities to demonstrate what they can do, and invest in those who bring both ability and the collaborative spirit required to build something extraordinary.

Bush said that when he recognized Weems as a multidisciplinary professional — animator, concept artist, storyboard artist and voice actor — “the decision to ink a multi-year deal was easy. I wanted her to have the creative freedom to contribute to the partnership in her own ways.”

“Zaria represents so much of what we want City Kidz to stand for,” he continued. “She is exceptionally talented, but she is also humble, kind, compassionate and generous in the way she works with other people. From the first time I experienced her energy and passion, I knew she was the person I wanted to bring Jazzy Duval to life.”

Bush sees the relationship as a two-way commitment. “We want Zaria to pour her talent into Jazzy, but City Kidz also has a responsibility to pour our expertise and support into Zaria,” he said. “We want to give her the creative space, professional experience, exposure and relationships that can help propel her career. When Zaria and Jazzy truly become one, I think people are going to understand just how special this young woman is.”

Weems’ creative journey began as a child in Austell, Georgia, where drawing, video games and animated characters opened the door to worlds she wanted to create herself. A digital drawing tablet from her grandmother helped turn that fascination into a serious pursuit. She later attended the Savannah College of Art and Design (SCAD) and was selected for a Disney internship opportunity that exposed her to accomplished artists and entertainment-industry professionals.

What attracted her to City Kidz was the chance to contribute rather than simply execute. “Having the creative freedom to really take Jazzy and help mold her is what made me so excited,” Weems said. “I get to immerse myself in her and think about who she is, how she sounds and how she comes alive.”

Bold, energetic and unmistakably Jacksonville, Jazzy is envisioned as one of the signature personalities audiences will encounter as the City Kidz universe expands across animated shorts, educational and social content and, ultimately, larger entertainment properties. As the crew’s resident newscaster, she also will be one of the faces and voices of City Kidz’s emerging Animating Jacksonville initiative.

Animating Jacksonville envisions the city itself as part of the studio’s animated universe. The Main Street Bridge, St. Johns River, Jacksonville neighborhoods, the Jaguars Stadium of the Future and other recognizable landmarks are being incorporated into original animated stories designed to take both City Kidz and Jacksonville to audiences around the world.

Zaria’s selection also demonstrates a larger ambition for City Kidz NexGen Animation Studios. Through its fellowship and expanding production operation, City Kidz is bringing emerging animators, artists, writers, voice performers and other creative professionals into real projects built around original intellectual property — giving them opportunities to do consequential work, earn credits, develop professional relationships and be seen.

The studio hopes Weems’ story will encourage other talented voice actors and creative professionals to look closely at what City Kidz is building and imagine themselves becoming part of it.

For Weems, the journey comes back to a piece of advice she frequently gives other young creatives: find your spark. “You don’t have to explain why you’re doing it,” Weems said. “Find what drives you and stand on it.”

“This is just the beginning,” Bush said. “Zaria is excited. We’re excited. And when people finally meet the Jazzy Duval that Zaria is helping us create, I think they’re going to realize we’re building something very different.”

Because Jazzy has something to say.

data.title: Cushman & Wakefield Report Shows U.S. Construction Cost Pressures Shift From Labor to Materials as Metals Prices Surge
data.description:
Cushman & Wakefield Report Shows U.S. Construction Cost Pressures Shift From Labor to Materials as Metals Prices Surge

Construction-related commodity prices rise 13.3% year-over-year as data centers and infrastructure sustain demand amid broader construction slowdown

U.S. construction cost pressures are shifting from labor to materials, with construction-related commodity prices rising 13.3% year-over-year (YOY) as tariffs, metals supply constraints and demand from data centers and infrastructure projects push input costs higher, according to Cushman & Wakefield’s latest Construction Insights for Global Occupiers report.

The increase in commodity prices is more than 4.7 times the rate recorded a year earlier, led by aluminum at 40.9%, copper base scrap at 39.3% and nonferrous metals at 38.5%. At the same time, labor cost growth has moderated, creating a markedly different construction inflation environment from recent years.

“The pressure on construction costs hasn’t disappeared, but its source is changing,” said Tyler Paytas, Global Head of Programs & Projects, Global Occupier Services at Cushman & Wakefield. “Labor remains constrained, particularly in specialized trades, but materials and equipment are increasingly driving escalation. For occupiers planning projects, that means the cost environment can remain challenging even as wage growth moderates.”

The ENR Building Cost Index increased 4.7% YOY in August, compared with a 1.5% increase in its skilled labor component. Overall construction materials rose at least 1.0% month over month for three consecutive months through August, with annual growth accelerating from 6.5% in June to 8.5% in August.

Electrical equipment is emerging as a particular pressure point. Electrical machinery and equipment prices increased 13.0% YOY, while switchgear increased 9.0%, reflecting demand from grid modernization, renewable energy investment and data center development. Transformer and switchgear costs are forecast to accelerate further through the end of the year amid continued copper supply constraints.

Data Centers Sustain Construction Activity as Broader Market Softens

The cost shift is occurring against an increasingly divided construction backdrop, with data centers and infrastructure projects supporting activity while many traditional commercial real estate sectors remain subdued.

Contractors working on data center projects reported an average backlog of 11.0 months, compared with 8.5 months among contractors without data center exposure. Infrastructure construction backlog reached 10.1 months in June, up 7.9% from a year earlier.

Meanwhile, commercial and industrial architectural billings registered 46.7 in June, below the 50 threshold indicating growth. Nine of the past 10 months have registered below 50, signaling continued weakness in the broader nonresidential construction pipeline into 2027.

“Construction is increasingly a story of two markets,” said Ethan Tribble, Senior Research Analyst, Global Research at Cushman & Wakefield. “Data centers, infrastructure and other large projects are generating significant demand for materials, electrical equipment and specialized labor even as pipelines remain much thinner across traditional sectors. That concentration is supporting overall construction activity while putting additional pressure on many of the same inputs occupiers need for their projects.”

The divergence is also contributing to greater volatility in national construction activity. New construction starts surged 33.5% month over month in May as major healthcare, manufacturing, utilities and data center projects broke ground, before declining 20% in June.

U.S. Cost Escalation Remains Muted, For Now

Despite rapidly rising input costs, overall U.S. construction cost growth has remained comparatively contained. Construction costs increased 0.7% from the fourth quarter of 2025, compared with 6.4% in South Korea and 3.9% in Germany.

Greater domestic energy production has helped insulate the U.S. from some of the energy-driven construction cost increases experienced in more import-dependent markets. However, Cushman & Wakefield expects U.S. construction prices to accelerate as higher materials and equipment costs increasingly flow through to project pricing.

Contractor pricing was up an average of 4.3% YOY as of June, including a 6.4% increase in concrete. Metro-level construction costs increased an average of 4.42% YOY during the second quarter, approximately 0.9 percentage points above the national producer price index for nonresidential structures.

“Cost escalation is increasingly concentrated in the materials and systems that are critical to modern construction,” Paytas said. “For occupiers, early procurement, realistic budgeting and understanding where those pressures are most acute will become increasingly important as projects move forward.”

Globally, supply chain pressures have eased from their April peak, but Cushman & Wakefield expects metals and equipment costs to remain elevated amid structural supply constraints. Infrastructure, energy and data center projects continue to drive construction activity, while development across many traditional commercial real estate sectors remains comparatively subdued.
